transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I’m here because I just keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. 

I work in retail, and... like, recently I completely yelled at one of my employees just for putting some stock on the wrong shelf. It was a huge overreaction. Afterward, I was actually shaking, because that is really not how I usually treat people. I just don't feel like myself, and I need to figure out what's going on.
Have you always struggled with these outbursts, or is this something that has only started happening recently?

No, I haven't always been like this at all. It's definitely a recent thing. Um... it's been going on for about two weeks now. It started right after we had a kitchen fire, back during our first weekend working on the house. Ever since then, I've just been having these outbursts.
Since the kitchen fire occurred, have you been having any unwanted, distressing memories or nightmares about that event?

Yes, actually. The fire just keeps jumping into my head out of nowhere. It's really upsetting. 

Like, I'll just be picking up a pan to make dinner, or even just opening a spreadsheet at work, and suddenly it's like I'm right back there. I can smell the smoke and I can see the kitchen filling up with it again. It happens so fast, and I can't seem to stop it from happening. It's really hard to deal with.

During these moments when you feel like you are back in the kitchen fire, are you still aware of your current surroundings, or does it feel like you have completely lost touch with the present moment?

Um... I'm not really sure, honestly. It all happens so fast. 

I don't know if I completely lose touch with where I am, but... the memory is just so overwhelming that I'm not really paying attention to my actual surroundings when it happens. I'm just so focused on the smoke and the panic in my head, I haven't really noticed how much I'm aware of the present moment.
When these memories happen, do you ever feel like you are actually reliving the fire as if it is happening all over again right now, rather than just remembering it as a past event?

No, I wouldn't say I feel like I'm actually reliving it right in the moment. It's more just... a really strong memory. Like I said, I can smell the smoke and see it in my head, but I know I'm not actually back in the fire. It's just a very intense memory of it.
